rv.q: Easily one of the finest works of the decade, "Downstate" is the best new play I've seen since, well, "Downstate."

Downstate is in no way a paean to pedophilia, but it prompts us to examine where justice ends and vengeance begins, to think about different kinds of power imbalance, and to extend our humanity in challenging directions.
This phenomenal piece of acting is matched by Francis Guinan, another holdover whose increased age has only deepened his work and whose gentleness stands in total contrast.
Playwright Norris builds the tension and momentum of Downstate almost entirely through character interaction... and yet the entire play is compelling from beginning to end.
This new Broadway version, steered by the veteran director Joe Mantello (Wicked, this year’s Death of a Salesman ) is a pyrotechnic display of acting prowess.
Downstate forces us to stand at the shore of our own reservoir of mercy, to consider how deep it really goes.
Freeman, giving the performance of a lifetime as Dee, dominates "Downstate."
Shame on me for missing the play then. Don't miss it now.
Downstate is not an easy play to watch. But it is a stunning achievement, meticulously constructed and emotionally devastating.
Norris is the demolition expert of the American theater, giving audiences an up-close look as our simplistic fairy tales implode onstage.
Bruce Norris doesn't let anyone off the hook in Downstate, on stage or off. It's what makes the play gut-wrenching, horrifying, difficult — and excellent.
That noted, the best play of 2022 is now the best revival to appear on Broadway in 2026.
If the Off-Broadway production was superbly acted and directed, the Broadway version is even better.
All in all, Downstate remains a play worth seeing (there isn't another one like it) and Mantello's production is finely calibrated.
Their initial exchange is, under Mr. Mantello's expert guidance, a master class in unsettling comedy...

vs.sum: The Booth Theatre offers good sightlines with a well-raked mezzanine and clear views from most seats, though legroom can be tight. The theater's elegant, European-inspired design adds to its charm, while sound quality is consistently praised. Facilities are average, with typical restroom and concession offerings.

acc.note: 6 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra. Not completely wheelchair accessible. Infrared devices available.
